alumni.name: John "Iron Mike" Harrington
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

John “Iron Mike” Harrington was a leading halfback and two-time co-captain during one of Saugus High’s strongest early eras. He contributed to the 1939 North Shore championship team and held the ball for Joe Bucherie’s decisive field goal in the 3–0 victory over Salem. The yearbooks identify him as a co-captain for both the 1940 and 1941 seasons.

As a senior in 1941, Harrington helped Henry Toczylowski’s Sachems win the Class C state championship. The season review pairs him with Ed Shipulski as the team’s “touchdown twins.” Harrington scored the tying touchdown in the closing minute against Leominster, broke scoring runs of 37 yards against Gloucester and 47 yards against Swampscott, and threw the late touchdown pass to Claude Collette that secured a 6–0 victory over Marblehead. His recognition included the Boston Globe’s 1941 All-Scholastic second team at back and its North Shore All-Scholastic eleven.

His 1942 senior biography records four years of football alongside participation in baseball, basketball, hockey and track. A later Saugus Advocate retrospective reports that a serious automobile accident after graduation curtailed his playing career and that he subsequently returned to Saugus as an assistant football coach.

alumni.name: Art Statuto
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1989.

Art Statuto’s career connected Saugus High’s championship years with Notre Dame and professional football. A member of the 1941 Class C state champions, he played center and contributed on defense as well as offense. The 1942 yearbook singled out his work against both the pass and the run in Saugus’ 26–0 victory over Revere. The Boston Globe’s 1941 selections listed him as an All-Scholastic honorable mention at center. His 1943 senior biography also records service as junior class president.

Statuto joined Notre Dame’s 1943 squad and later returned to the Irish after wartime Navy service. Notre Dame’s 1946 Football Review describes 37 months in the Navy, service as an engineering officer aboard a landing ship, and football with the Fort Pierce Navy team. He was part of Notre Dame’s celebrated 1946 and 1947 national championship squads. A university retrospective identifies him as a reserve center whose subsequent professional success reflected the remarkable depth of those teams. The Saugus Advocate also records his selection to the 1948 College Football All-Star Team.

He went on to play center for the Buffalo Bills of the All-America Football Conference in 1948 and 1949 and the Los Angeles Rams of the NFL in 1950. His Rams career is also preserved in the promotional football card in this archive.

alumni.name: Doug Waybright
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1988.

Doug Waybright was a member of Saugus’ 1941 Class C state championship squad and developed into a versatile back and team leader. In his senior season of 1943, he shared the captaincy with Jim MacDougall and earned selection to the Essex County All-Star squad for its meeting with Greater Boston at Manning Bowl.

The yearbook’s 1943 season account highlights his impact on both sides of the ball. In the 32–7 victory over Newburyport, Waybright scored two early touchdowns and added a 67-yard interception return for another score. Other accounts credit him with an interception against Marblehead and a long punt return against Wakefield that was called back, illustrating the range of ways he could change a game.

At Notre Dame, Waybright moved to end and was a member of the 1947 and 1949 national championship teams. The university’s 1948 Football Review reports that he resumed his Irish career in 1947 after two years in the infantry and had earned two Notre Dame monograms by the end of 1948. Notre Dame’s draft history also lists his selection by Buffalo in the 1948 AAFC draft, before his final national championship season with the Irish in 1949.

His Saugus legacy extended to youth sports and community service. A later hometown retrospective recalls his work with young athletes and the naming of the Waybright elementary school in his memory after his death at age 38.

alumni.name: Art Spinney
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

Went on to play college football at Boston College where he was Captain his senior season (1949). A 1972 Inductee into the Boston College Athletic Hall of Fame.
Played in the NFL for the Baltimore Colts (1950, 1953-1960) where he won several accolades:
3x All Pro (1958 - 1960)
2x Pro Bowl (1959 - 1960)
2x NFL Champion (1958 - 1959)
Was the Offensive Line Coach for the Boston Patriots from 1962 - 1968.

Before his college and professional career, Spinney captained Saugus’ undefeated 1944 Class B state championship team. The preserved 1944 North Shore All-Star roster lists him at end. The gallery also follows his transition to Boston College, including a 1946 action photograph against Alabama and the announcement of his election as BC’s 1949 captain.

alumni.name: George Laskey
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

George Laskey was a powerful runner whose football honors span both the 1946 and 1947 seasons. The preserved 1946 North Shore All-Star roster lists him at halfback. As a senior in 1947, he earned the Lynn Item’s All-Scholastic selection at fullback and recognition on the Boston Post’s All-Scholastic team.

Laskey’s running figures prominently in the yearbooks’ game accounts. In 1946 he scored the touchdown and conversion in Saugus’ 7–0 victory over Peabody and helped produce wins over Swampscott and Marblehead. Under new coach John Janusas in 1947, he remained a central part of the attack alongside quarterback Earle Dudman and fellow backs Ernie Anganis and Frank Forti. The season review describes his kickoff return and running in the comeback victory over Chelsea and his scoring contributions against Swampscott.

His recognition continued beyond the school schedule. A Boston Post photograph dated December 8, 1947 shows Laskey scoring on a two-yard plunge for the North Shore All-Stars at Manning Bowl in their victory over Suburban Boston. A later awards report identifies him as the 1947 recipient of the Thomas R. Atkins Memorial Trophy. His 1948 senior biography records four years of football participation, preserving the school career behind those regional honors.

alumni.name: Dan Murphy
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1994.

Dan “Danny” Murphy was a guard and co-captain, alongside Salvatore “Sardi” Nicolo, on John Janusas’ 1949 North Shore co-championship and Exchange Bowl championship team. The Sachems finished 10–1, closing the season with their dramatic 7–6 victory over Weymouth. Murphy’s role at the line of scrimmage helped provide the foundation for a backfield featuring the Nicolo brothers and Fred Quinlan.

His senior season brought widespread recognition. His honors included Boston Globe All-Scholastic recognition in 1949, along with Lynn Item and Boston Sunday Post selections at guard. The Post’s November 27, 1949 page includes his portrait among its All-Scholastic players. A separate school awards clipping identifies Murphy as the team’s outstanding lineman and records the presentation of his trophy alongside Nicolo’s backfield award.

Murphy’s leadership extended beyond football. His 1950 senior biography identifies him as senior class president, a four-year football participant and senior co-captain, with additional participation in baseball, hockey and track. The 1949 “A family affair” clipping also pairs him with his younger brother Charlie among the six sets of brothers on the Sachems’ squad. Together, the yearbook and newspaper pages preserve a player who represented Saugus as a lineman, captain and student leader.

alumni.name: Salvatore 'Sardi' Nicolo
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

A three-year starter at running back, Sal “Sardi” Nicolo became one of Massachusetts’ most celebrated high school football players. In a memorable senior season, he led his division in touchdowns and points, earned numerous All-Scholastic selections and received honorable mention High School All-American recognition.

His signature Sachems moment came in the 1949 Exchange Bowl, when he caught a 50-yard, over-the-shoulder touchdown pass from his brother Richie to tie Weymouth as time expired. Jimmy Kane’s extra point secured Saugus’ 7–6 victory and the Exchange Bowl championship. Nicolo also excelled in baseball.

He went on to play football at Louisiana State University from 1952 through 1954. His 94-yard touchdown run against Rice on October 4, 1952, remains a memorable achievement in LSU football history.

Three Generations of Sachems Football

Salvatore “Sardi” Nicolo’s football legacy at Saugus High School has continued through three generations of his family. His son, John Nicolo (Class of 1976), became a standout Sachems player, earning multiple All-Scholastic selections and Player of the Year honors. John went on to win a national championship at Ithaca College, where he also earned All-American recognition.

John’s sons, Sal and Mike Nicolo, carried on the family tradition in the early 2000s. Sal was a two-way starter at fullback and linebacker during the 2001 and 2002 seasons. Mike distinguished himself over four seasons with the Sachems, earning multiple All-Scholastic honors and setting what was then the school’s single-game rushing record.

Together, Sardi, John, Sal, and Mike represent three generations of dedication, achievement, and lasting contributions to Saugus football history.

Salvatore “Sardi” Nicolo, his son John and his grandson Mike represent three generations of Sachems football and Saugus High Athletic Hall of Fame inductees. John’s sons Sal and Mike both played for Saugus. Sal was a two-way starter at fullback and linebacker in 2001 and 2002.

alumni.name: Richard “Richie” Nicolo
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1988.

A Lynn Item All-Scholastic in 1950, Richard “Richie” Nicolo was a dual-threat quarterback who could beat opponents with both his arm and his legs. He led the Sachems to consecutive Exchange Bowl championships in 1949 and 1950.

In the 1949 Exchange Bowl, his 50-yard touchdown pass to his brother Sardi as time expired tied Weymouth. Jimmy Kane’s extra point completed the dramatic 7–6 victory. The following year, Richie threw two touchdown passes and rushed for two more scores in a 30–12 win over Brockton, earning the game’s Most Valuable Player honors.

Nicolo continued his college football career at Boston College and Louisiana State University (LSU).

alumni.name: Christie Serino
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

Set the career passing yards record at Saugus.
Went on to have a successful hockey coaching career. Coached in the Hockey East 1991 - 2005 (Assistant Coach at UNH 1991-1998; Head Coach at Merrimack 1999 - 2005).
Spent his final years as head coach, building Malden Catholic hockey program into a powerhouse (2005 - 2011). He led Malden Catholic to the Super 8 Championship in his final season in 2011.

Serino’s Saugus career extended across football, hockey and baseball. The 1967 graduate later competed in all three sports at American International College. The Saugus Advocate’s retrospective credits him with more than 4,000 passing yards at Saugus and identifies him as the Sachems’ 1967 MVP in all three sports. Saugus’ high-school stadium was subsequently named in his honor.

alumni.name: Doug Mackie
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

2x Boston Globe, Boston Herald, and Lynn Item All Scholastic (1974-1975). Named to Parade Magazine and Blue Chip Magazine High School All American Team in 1975. Went on to play college football at Ohio State for the legendary Woody Hayes. Injuries cost him some playing time during his college days. Went on to play professionally in the NFL for the New York Giants (1982), New Orleans Saints (1986), and Atlanta Falcons (1987) although he was mostly a practice player in the NFL. His greatest success as a professional was in the USFL where he played for the Tampa Bay Bandits (1983) and the New Jersey Generals (1984-1985). While playing for the New Jersey Generals he was selected as a 1984 College & Pro Football Newsweekly 2nd Team All-Pro along with running back Herschel Walker as he was part of the starting offensive line who helped Walker set the still standing, single-season, pro football rushing record of 2,411 yards.

The January 12, 1976 Boston Globe recruiting feature identifies Mackie as the paper’s Player of the Year and describes his meetings with Ohio State coach Woody Hayes. The Item’s 1999 “Century’s Top 100 Players” series ranked him No. 19 on its list spanning multiple sports, preserving his standing among the area’s outstanding athletes.

alumni.name: Steve Gannon
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1988.

Went on to play college football at Holy Cross. He was a standout member of the defense for the Holy Cross football team during the late 1970s. Earned first team All-ECAC honors during his senior year, in addition to receiving the Davitt Award as the team’s top defensive lineman. As a senior led the team with 143 tackles, the most in recorded school history at the time. During his junior year in 1978, he helped lead the Crusaders to an overall record of 7-4, including victories over Air Force, Army and Boston College. A 2020 Inductee into the Holy Cross Athletic Hall of Fame. After college he had two NFL tryouts, one with the New York Giants and one with the Cincinnati Bengals both in 1980. After his playing days ended he got involved in coaching youth and high school football, being an assistant coach on John Nicolo's Sachems teams (2001-2004).

His Saugus contributions included both defense and fullback play. A junior-season Item capsule credits him with 512 rushing yards, blocking for John Nicolo and four team defensive-player-of-the-week honors in eight games. The archive also preserves his Holy Cross signing feature and a senior college profile describing the professional scouting interest his defensive-end play attracted.

The Gannon family’s Sachems football tradition continued with Steve’s sons, Rob Gannon and John Gannon. Rob started at wide receiver and defensive back in 2002, then at quarterback and defensive back in 2003 and 2004. John played on the Saugus offensive and defensive lines during the 2001 and 2002 seasons.

alumni.name: John Nicolo
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1987.

A two-time Lynn Item All-Scholastic (1974, 1975) and 1975 Thom McAn North Shore Player of the Year and Boston Herald All-Scholastic, he captained Saugus to a share of the 1975 Northeastern Conference championship. A contemporary report of his first varsity opportunity against Danvers in 1973 describes long runs that helped set up two touchdowns. His 1975 season culminated in the Item sports staff's outstanding-football-player selection and the Thom McAn Shoe Award. The Item later ranked him No. 20 in its 1999 “Century's Top 100 Players” series, covering multiple sports.

At Ithaca College, Nicolo was a four-year letterwinner in both football and baseball. A three-year starting running back, he compiled 1,817 rushing yards and 20 touchdowns, earned All-East and All-Conference honors in 1978 and 1979, and was a 1979 All-American and captain of Ithaca's NCAA Division III national championship football team, which defeated Wittenberg 14–10 in the Stagg Bowl.

The following spring, as senior captain and shortstop, he helped Ithaca win the 1980 NCAA Division III baseball national championship. He went 5-for-6 with three RBI in the 12–5 title-game victory over Marietta and was named College World Series Most Valuable Player after setting tournament records with 12 hits and nine runs. He earned All-World Series recognition in 1978 and 1980, All-East baseball honors in 1979 and 1980, and conference baseball Player of the Year honors in each of his final two seasons. He received Ithaca's 1980 Ben Light Award as Male Athlete of the Year.

Following graduation, Nicolo played professional minor-league baseball for the Auburn Americans in 1980. He is a three-time Ithaca College Athletic Hall of Fame inductee: individually in 1986, with the 1979 football championship team in 2014, and with the 1980 baseball championship team in 2019.

He later helped rebuild the Saugus Pop Warner program, served as Saugus Sachems head football coach from 2001 to 2004, and was interim Saugus High School Athletic Director from 2003 to 2004.

alumni.name: Steve Peach
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1991.

Steve Peach was Saugus’ versatile quarterback, safety and kicking specialist and the first player to earn three Item football All-Star selections, in 1978, 1979 and 1980. Later Item team announcements identify him as the original three-time selection. His 1981 senior biography also records captaincies in football and baseball and three years of basketball.

The newspaper capsules trace his development. As a sophomore in 1978, he passed for 1,050 yards and 11 touchdowns, ran for three scores and intercepted four passes. In 1979 he completed 108 of 206 passes for 1,489 yards and 14 touchdowns, added four rushing touchdowns, kicked a 48-yard field goal and averaged 39 yards per punt. On defense, he led the Sachems with six interceptions and three fumble recoveries. His 1980 senior capsule credits him with 1,200 passing yards, eight touchdown passes and eight touchdowns scored, plus a 38-yard punting average.

Peach was selected for the North squad in the 1981 Shriners Football Classic, whose Boston Globe preview noted his Syracuse scholarship. He subsequently played at Syracuse before transferring to Boston College. BC’s official record book lists him at quarterback/punter in 1984 and 1985, and a hometown retrospective recalls his role as Doug Flutie’s backup and the Eagles’ Cotton Bowl punter. His career stands out for its combination of passing, defense, kicking and participation in three high-school sports.

alumni.name: Darren McCullough
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1997.

Darren McCullough ranks among the best all-around players in Sachems history and is one of the few Saugus players to earn Lynn Item All-Scholastic honors twice.

As a junior in 1985, he recorded 123 tackles and four interceptions while playing linebacker and defensive back. On offense, he rushed for 442 yards and added 232 receiving yards, finishing with six total touchdowns.

As a senior in 1986, McCullough again led the team in tackles and rushed for 1,081 yards and 11 touchdowns. His standout performance came against Danvers, when he rushed for 225 yards and four touchdowns while also making 16 tackles. That effort earned him the Item/Coca-Cola Gold Helmet Award.

alumni.name: Marc Fauci
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2000.

A 2x Lynn Item All Scholastic. Boston Globe All Scholastic his senior season. Won the NEC Most Valuable Player Award in football during his senior year. A 2x co-captain as a junior and senior. Went on to play college football for Boston University. Led the Terriers football team during arguably its best season ever in 1993 when BU went 12-1 and finished the regular season with a perfect 11-0 mark, the first unbeaten and untied record in program history. A second-team All-America selection by The Sports Network and National Weekly Football Gazette and a third-team All-America selection by the Associated Press, Fauci played linebacker and ranks in the top five for career primary, assisted and total tackles. Was a 2010 Inductee into the Boston University Athletic Hall of Fame.

His senior Item capsule provides a detailed measure of that impact: 440 career tackles and 19 interceptions, with the team tackle lead in three consecutive seasons. In 1989 he averaged 14 tackles per game, recovered four fumbles and contributed 757 rushing yards and 743 passing yards on offense. The capsule also credits him with four career Gold Helmet awards, honor-roll standing and three terms as class president.

alumni.name: Dan Schena
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2001.

Dan Schena was a senior tri-captain and standout on both lines for Saugus’ 8–2 team in 1990. Alongside fellow captains Ryan Magnasco and Chris Mikulski, he helped lead the final Sachems team coached by Kevin Ward. The 1991 yearbook credits that squad with 288 points, surpassing the previous school season mark of 284, and seven Northeastern Conference All-Stars.

Schena’s own 1990 Lynn Item All-Star capsule describes a 6-foot-3, 240-pound lineman with unusual speed: he was the team’s third-fastest player. He made more than 100 tackles, earned NEC All-Star recognition and anchored a defense whose strength began up front. Ward’s assessment placed him among the program’s outstanding linemen since Doug Mackie.

The yearbook remembers the team’s closeness with its coaches as well as its victories, placing Schena within a senior class celebrated for both achievement and shared memories. He continued his football career at Northeastern University, whose official all-time lettermen list records varsity letters in each season from 1992 through 1995. Those four college seasons extend a football career that began with distinction on both sides of the line at Saugus.

alumni.name: Mike Mabee
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2006.

Mike Mabee was a senior co-captain, quarterback and defensive contributor at the center of Saugus’ 1995 revival. A multisport athlete and Lynn Item football All-Star, he helped the Sachems end a 34-game losing streak and finish 6–5, their first winning season since 1990.

His 1995 Item capsule records an efficient passing season: 61 completions in 95 attempts for 720 yards and six touchdowns. He also carried 60 times for 360 yards and seven touchdowns. His impact extended to defense, where he was the team’s second-leading tackler and recorded six interceptions and two fumble recoveries. A leg injury limited him during part of the season; the capsule emphasizes the difference his availability made to the offense.

Mabee helped deliver two defining victories. In the 25–0 win over Winthrop that ended the losing streak, he threw for a touchdown as Saugus combined a productive offense with two critical defensive stands near its goal line. Later, in the 50–20 win over Lynn English at Manning Bowl that secured a winning season, he threw two touchdown passes, ran for a score and intercepted two passes. Those performances capture the breadth of his contribution: he could direct the offense, gain yards himself and help take the ball away on defense.

alumni.name: LJ McKanas
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2007.

Captain his senior season. Played a big role in turning Saugus into a competitive program in the mid-90s. During his senior season he set records for most rushing yards and most touchdowns. He was selected Boston Globe, Boston Herald, and Lynn Item All-Scholastic. He then went on to play college football at Northeastern University. After he redshirted his freshman season, he went on to become a four-year starter. During his redshirt freshman season he broke the NU rookie rushing record with 832 yards, averaging 92.4 yards per game. His Sophomore and Junior seasons were derailed due to injuries. During his senior season he set school records for most carries, 342, rushing yards, 1756, and rushing touchdowns, 14. For his senior season, he was named team MVP, All-New England, All-Conference and first-team Hanson All-America. He was also the winner of the Harry Agganis Award as the Outstanding Senior Football Player in New England. After college he appeared on the TV Show "Survivor" in 2014 where he finished in 9th place.

His 1996 Item senior capsule names him NEC Offensive Player of the Year and credits him with 1,365 rushing yards, 20 rushing touchdowns, 424 receiving yards, two kickoff-return touchdowns and two Gold Helmet awards. His impact had already been evident in the 1995 breakthrough against Winthrop: he rushed for 178 yards and two touchdowns in the 25–0 win that ended Saugus’ 34-game losing streak.

alumni.name: Anthony “Beave” Barbanti
alumni.bio:
A two-time Lynn Item All-Scholastic, Anthony “Beave” Barbanti was a three-year starter on both the offensive and defensive lines and a cornerstone of the Sachems during his junior and senior seasons.

His senior season in 2003 was his finest: he recorded 75 tackles, including 11 tackles for loss, and three sacks. He was equally dominant on the offensive line, helping clear the way for Mike Nicolo’s record-setting rushing performances. Barbanti’s strength, consistency and two-way play made him a key part of Saugus’ success.

The 2003 Item capsule identifies Barbanti as a senior co-captain and a three-time Northeastern Conference All-Star, in addition to his two Item selections. His 2002 junior capsule had already described him as a two-year starter whom the coaches regarded as their best player throughout that season.
alumni.source: Profile supplied by Sal Nicolo; senior statistics corroborated by the 2003 Item All-Star clipping.

alumni.name: Mike Nicolo
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee (Class of 2026). A four-year starter and team captain his senior year, he set a then–single-game rushing record with 306 yards against Salem as a junior. He earned Lynn Item All-Scholastic honors that same season. Though injuries limited his senior year, his athletic success extended beyond football—he was an All-Scholastic selection in Winter Track as a sophomore and in Baseball as a junior.
He continued his football career at Curry College, where he was part of four consecutive New England Football Conference championship teams. He also contributed to Curry’s first-ever NCAA Division III playoff victory—fittingly, against his father John’s alma mater, Ithaca College.

With his induction into the Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame in 2026, Mike joins his grandfather, Salvatore “Sardi” Nicolo, and his father, John Nicolo, in the Hall. Together, they become the first three generations of one family to be inducted into the school’s Athletic Hall of Fame—a milestone in the Nicolo family’s Saugus sports legacy. His brother Sal was a two-way starter for the Sachems at fullback and linebacker in 2001 and 2002.

alumni.name: Brett Reid
alumni.bio:
A three-year starting quarterback and two-time Lynn Item All-Scholastic, Brett Reid helped lead a resurgence in Sachems football. As a junior in 2007, he teamed with Tyler Trainor, Paul Sullivan and Mike Dean to guide Saugus to a 7–3 record—its first winning season since 1997 and its most wins since 1996.

Operating in a run-heavy offense, Reid rushed for 797 yards and 13 touchdowns that season. He and Dean helped Saugus repeat its 7–3 finish in 2008, with Reid contributing 800 rushing yards and 12 touchdowns.

His senior Item capsule also identifies Reid as a captain and a two-time Northeastern Conference All-Star. As a junior, he directed an option offense that the paper credited with averaging 23 points per game. The consecutive Item selections recognize his importance as both the offense’s decision-maker and a productive runner.
alumni.source: Profile details supplied by Sal Nicolo, October 2026.

alumni.name: Justin Winn
alumni.bio:
Justin Winn earned Lynn Item All-Scholastic honors in both his junior and senior seasons. In 2013, he scored 19 rushing touchdowns (the statistics table lists 1,103 rushing yards; the supplied alumni text lists 1,108, a difference still under review), providing a standout individual performance during a difficult 3–8 season for the Sachems.

In 2014, Winn and running back Dan Cicciola helped lead Saugus to a 6–5 record. Winn rushed for 1,255 yards and set a school record with 22 rushing touchdowns.

His senior Item capsule also identifies him as a captain and Northeastern Conference All-Star and records a five-touchdown performance against Lynn English.
alumni.source: Profile details supplied by Sal Nicolo, October 2026.

alumni.name: Braden Faiella
alumni.bio:
A two-time captain and two-time Lynn Item All-Star, Braden Faiella was the Item’s Defensive Player of the Year as a senior in 2023. His junior capsule reports 184 tackles; his senior profile records 140 tackles and a career total of 482. That final season also included an interception returned for a touchdown, five forced fumbles and four fumble recoveries. He contributed on the offensive line as well as at linebacker.

He continued his career at Saint Anselm College, whose 2026 roster lists him as a junior linebacker from Saugus.
alumni.source: Profile details supplied by Sal Nicolo, October 2026.

alumni.name: Carlo Abate
alumni.bio:
Carlo Abate was a three-year starting linebacker and a defensive leader during Saugus’ rebuilding years of the mid-1990s. He earned Lynn Item All-Star and Northeastern Conference All-Star recognition in both 1994 and 1995, combining consistent tackling with an ability to create turnovers.

As a junior in 1994, Abate led his team and the area with more than 120 tackles. His Item capsule highlights 22 tackles against Lynn English, which earned him a Gold Helmet award, and another 19 stops against Lynn Classical. Those performances established him as one of the region’s most productive young linebackers.

As a senior in 1995, he overcame knee and shoulder injuries to lead the Sachems with 115 tackles, adding four interceptions and four fumble recoveries. His contribution was central to a season of renewal: Saugus ended its 34-game losing streak with a 25–0 victory over Winthrop and finished 6–5 for its first winning season since 1990. The report of the breakthrough win credits Abate with 14 tackles and identifies him and Dan Vass as pillars of the defense. His two Item capsules preserve both the individual production and the resilience behind that team turnaround.

alumni.name: Edward “Eddie” Shipulski
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1988.

Edward “Eddie” Shipulski was a major backfield star during one of Saugus High's finest football eras. A three-season player, he helped the Sachems win the 1939 North Shore championship and the 1941 Class C state championship. The 1940 yearbook singled him out as a sophomore standout after he scored twice in a 26–0 victory over Gloucester. By his senior season, Shipulski and Mike Harrington formed the backfield partnership the yearbook called its “touchdown twins.” Shipulski's 1941 highlights included touchdown runs of 70 yards against Gloucester, 57 yards against Amesbury, and 87 yards against Swampscott. A newspaper preview credited him with a team-leading 84 points entering Thanksgiving, despite an arm injury that limited his late-season action. He received Boston Globe All-Scholastic honorable mention and also played varsity baseball.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Michael “Mike” Garofano
alumni.bio: Michael Garofano helped lead Saugus High's return to organized football in 1914. A September newspaper feature identified him as captain and left halfback of a team being rebuilt after a lengthy interruption. By the time of a 1917 preseason report, Garofano was serving in France during World War I, and Saugus was preparing to select a replacement captain. His surviving clippings preserve both an early leader of the revived football program and a young Saugus serviceman whose life extended beyond the playing field.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Franklin “Oozo” Pike
alumni.bio: Franklin Pike was a powerful, versatile fullback at the center of Fred Beresford's unbeaten 1922 Saugus team. Contemporary coverage praised his strength as a runner and his ability to pass and kick, making him a threat in several parts of the game. He had already attracted notice in 1921, when a 75-yard interception return helped Saugus defeat Rockland. A later profile credited him with decisive performances against Rockland and Wellesley and described his development into one of the team's leading players. Pike represents the early generation that helped establish Saugus as a competitive football program.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Edward Amery
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1992.

Captain Edward Amery supplied leadership and versatility to Saugus High's unbeaten 1922 eleven. The contemporary profile of the team praised him as a passer, receiver, interceptor, and its leading punter. Alongside Franklin Pike, Lester Pool, and quarterback Forest Kenerson, Amery helped give a relatively light squad the skill and adaptability to compete successfully under Fred Beresford. His captaincy and contributions in several roles helped shape one of Saugus's earliest outstanding teams.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: John “Jack” Leahy
alumni.bio: John Leahy was a captain and fullback during Albion Rice's early years at Saugus. A newspaper feature compared his summer work delivering heavy blocks of ice with the conditioning associated with football celebrity Red Grange. The article identified Leahy as a junior and one of Rice's leading hopes for the following fall. The later yearbook account places him among the experienced players around whom the successful 1927 team was built, preserving his importance as both a backfield player and a veteran leader. He was inducted into the Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame in 1992.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Reginald “Reggie” Goss
alumni.bio: Reggie Goss was an experienced leader of Saugus football in the late 1920s. After contributing at end to the 1927 team that won seven of eleven games, he was elected captain for 1928. The yearbook records his work at quarterback and end, his responsibility for the team's punting, and his determination despite an injury carried over from the previous season. In the muddy Thanksgiving game against Mission High, he caught Stuart Kidder's long pass and continued downfield on a play that gained more than sixty yards. The account also recognizes Goss's academic achievement.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: James “Jim” Foley
alumni.bio: Jim Foley earned a memorable place in the 1928 yearbook through his passing, tackling, and upbeat approach to football. Playing with one arm, he was praised for his judgment and effectiveness as well as his determination. The season account lists him among the quarterbacks and commends his backfield work against a heavier Mission High team on Thanksgiving. Foley's story offers a distinctive portrait of an early Saugus player whose teammates valued his ability, attitude, and willingness to take on the game's demands.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Stuart Kidder
alumni.bio: Stuart Kidder made a strong impression at fullback during the 1928 season. He won the fullback position and, according to the yearbook, gained more yardage than any other Saugus player that fall. His most vividly recalled play came against Mission High on Thanksgiving, when he escaped pressure and threw a long pass to Reggie Goss for a gain exceeding sixty yards. The yearbook regarded his combination of running ability and promise as one of the bright spots of a demanding season.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: James “Jim” Muzzy
alumni.bio: James Muzzy was a versatile halfback and captain of Saugus High's 1930 football team. When the lettermen elected him, Coach Albion Rice described him as the squad's best all-around player. The yearbook tribute credited Muzzy with consistent running, blocking, tackling, and passing, and ranked him behind only Laurie Templeman as a scoring threat. His leadership helped define a team remembered in the yearbook as Saugus's best since the unbeaten 1922 eleven.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Laurence “Laurie” Templeman
alumni.bio: Laurence “Laurie” Templeman was one of Saugus High's outstanding running threats at the turn of the 1930s. In 1929, he scored both touchdowns in the 12–0 victory over Swampscott that the yearbook described as Saugus's first football win over that opponent. He also scored three long touchdowns in a victory over Rockport. The following season's tribute praised his speed, scoring, and ability to threaten opponents whenever he carried the ball. Together with captain Jim Muzzy, Templeman gave Coach Rice an accomplished backfield pairing.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Charles “Charlie” Murphy
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 1999.

Charles Murphy was one of Saugus High's most widely recognized linemen of the early 1950s. A co-captain of the 1951 team, he earned places on the Boston Globe, Boston Post, and Lynn Item All-Scholastic selections. The Globe's main team identified him at guard, while the Item listed him as a senior guard. R.A.A. award material provides further recognition of his line play. These surviving selections document Murphy's distinction during the years immediately following the Exchange Bowl teams.
alumni.source: Contemporary newspaper clippings and Saugus yearbooks.

alumni.name: Jim Driscoll
alumni.bio:
Saugus High School Athletic Hall of Fame inductee, Class of 2006.

Jim Driscoll was a Lynn Item All-Scholastic halfback on Saugus High's 1950 Exchange Bowl championship team. His versatility helped the Sachems early in the season, when he moved to quarterback while Richie Nicolo was unavailable. The Football Folio records his passing connection with Charlie Woodell and his later contributions as a runner. Driscoll helped give the 8–2 Sachems an adaptable backfield during the season that ended with a 30–12 Exchange Bowl victory over Brockton.

Tony Serino contributed to the backfield during Saugus's successful transition from the Exchange Bowl years into the early 1950s. The 1950 Football Folio records two touchdown runs against Chelsea during the season that produced a second consecutive Exchange Bowl championship. In 1951, he shared the captaincy with Charlie Murphy and earned Lynn Item All-Scholastic recognition as a utility back. His scoring, leadership, and regional selection marked his contributions during these seasons.

The 1954 yearbook records four years of football participation and identifies Belyea and Bill Whittredge as first-string selections on the Lynn All-Star team. The Boston Globe also named Belyea among its All-Scholastic reserves at guard in December 1953. His individual recognition complemented his contributions to a championship team.

His leadership helped define a season capped by a decisive Thanksgiving win over Peabody and remembered as a championship autumn for the school.

John Dancewicz was a co-captain of Saugus High's 7–2 football team in 1966 and a first-team Lynn Item All-Star. Hanson's captaincy links the early years of Buzz Harvey's program with the greater success that followed in 1939.

David Russell Mathews was a football and hockey co-captain at Saugus High and a four-year participant in football, hockey and baseball. His senior yearbook remembered his broad athletic ability, and the football portrait collection preserves him among the leaders of Saugus's recognized 1959 championship team. The 1969 yearbook's football roster identifies him as a captain during a season in which Saugus recovered from a difficult start to finish with three consecutive victories.
